{"id":"78fa9d71-2dc5-4814-94f4-1d696d5b3901","object":"chat.completion","created":1790510293,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"parent_requirement_id": "R5", "mode": "probe", "used_claims": [], "local_residual": "Establish the existence and identity of the journal article by the author that was published six years after the book and on a topic similar to the book."}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need analyze. We have original question. Parent requirement R5: "then published a journal article on a similar topic six years after publishing the book." We need identify one current local research residual inside parent requirement, given no verified claims. Mode probe, used_claims []. Need choose one faithful low-commitment facet. We need not solve whole. Need maybe target the journal article published six years after the book, on similar topic, by the author. But since no claims, perhaps establish identity of book? Wait parent requirement is about "then published a journal article on a similar topic six years after publishing the book." It refers to "the book" from previous? Parent requirement source span Q3. Need local residual. Since no substantive supporting Claim, mode probe. local_residual should be one exploratory evidence objective. Must not be search query. Need preserve roles etc.

We need decide what facet. Parent Requirement includes conditions: (1) there is a journal article; (2) published by [the author] (subject from earlier); (3) on a similar topic [to the book]; (4) six years after publishing the book. With no claims, choose one coherent part. Could choose: establish the existence/identity of the journal article published six years after the book by the author, on similar topic. But that's essentially whole parent. Maybe one coherent facet: the identity/title of the journal article that the author published six years after the book. But question asks title; parent requirement is to establish that article. Since no evidence, probe this. Need not include search query. "Determine the journal article (title) published by the Indian author six years after the book, on a topic similar to the book." That is not search query. But maybe too broad? It's one coherent objective.

But instruction: If no substantive supporting Claim, use mode probe and local_residual is one exploratory evidence objective. So fine.

Need JSON with parent_requirement_id "R5", mode "probe", used_claims [], local_residual. Ensure no extra.

Should we mention "the author" not known? We can refer to subject described in original question? Local residual: "Establish whether there exists a journal article authored by the same author, published six years after the book, and on a topic similar to the book." That preserves relation.

Could maybe focus on the temporal relation: "the publication date of the journal article relative to the book publication is six years later." But parent includes similar topic. If no claims, one facet. The instruction says choose exactly one coherent evidence objective inside Parent Requirement. The parent requirement is a single condition? It has multiple semantic conditions but they are part of one article. We can choose "identify the journal article ..." as objective. It bundles similar topic and six years later? Hmm "Do not bundle independent research objectives." Are these independent? They are attributes of same article. But to identify the article, one needs both. However we can choose one part: "Establish the identity of the journal article on a similar topic that the author published six years after the book." That's the parent requirement itself, not a subpart. Since no part supported, an exploratory objective can be the whole? They said "If no substantive part of the Parent Requirement is supported yet, still choose one faithful, low-commitment facet of the Parent Requirement." So should be a facet, not whole. Could choose the journal article itself. It is a facet: the article's existence/identity. But it references "similar topic" and "six years after" as qualifiers. If we drop them, not faithful? We can say "Determine the identity/title of the journal article referred to by the condition that it was published six years after the book, while preserving the similar-topic relation as a constraint to be checked later." Hmm.

Maybe better: "Establish the existence and identity of the journal article that the author published six years after the book (the 'similar topic' relation to the book remaining to be verified)." But that's still bundling? It includes six-year relation. Alternatively choose "Establish the identity of the book whose publication is the reference point for the six-year interval." But book may be from previous requirement? Parent requirement says "after publishing the book" but parent is about article. The book is a prior entity. However R5 likely assumes book known from earlier. But if no claims, book unknown. Yet original question mentions "The author published a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing their PhD". Parent R5 concerns article six years after book. The residual could be "the journal article" not book. But if book not established, we might need book identity as prerequisite. However Parent Requirement R5 is specifically about the article. We should not jump to downstream? The article is downstream from book. But parent requirement itself is downstream. We can target the article. But if book identity unknown, maybe cannot establish six years after book. But the task is to identify one residual inside R5. Since no claims, the most direct is the journal article.

Need maybe no search query. "Identify the journal article on a similar topic that the author published six years after the book." That's an evidence objective. It is not a search query. But it's basically the answer? The original question asks title. The parent requirement is that the article exists and its relation. Our residual is to establish that article. Good.

Let's craft JSON.

Need maybe used_claims empty. mode probe. local_residual maybe: "Establish the identity of the journal article by the author that was published six years after the book and on a topic similar to the book." That is one sentence.

But "similar topic" and "six years after" are constraints. It's one coherent objective.

Should we mention "title"? The parent requirement doesn't explicitly ask title, but original question does. The local residual could be "the identity/title of that article". The instruction says do not jump to downstream attribute whose referent still needs to be established. But here the referent is the article. Title is an attribute. If article not established, we should establish the article, not title. However the original question asks title. Parent requirement is about the article's publication. The local residual should be the article itself, not title. So avoid "title" maybe. Say "Establish the existence/identity of the journal article..." That is referent, not downstream attribute. But if we say identity, that's okay. Title could be part of identity? Maybe.
